title: Inviting trouble
explanation: The speaker imagines someone summoning the very trouble they could have avoided. Used ironically, it criticises an unnecessary provocation or a knowingly risky decision. It should not be used to blame someone for harm they did not choose.
usage_example: A person interrupts an argument that has nothing to do with them merely to insult both sides; a friend may use this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: ବଳଦ is rendered here as ox or bullock. The horned animal supplies the force of the image; the wording alone cannot establish a particular village, farming community or date of origin.
